The only use outside the file is Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/FreeModule/Finite/Quotient.lean:77, which calls Submodule.quotientPi directly. The simp lemmas piQuotientLift_mk, piQuotientLift_single and quotientPiLift_mk look fine: each has a canonical left-hand side and a smaller right-hand side. The main concern is the @[simp] attribute on the auxiliary defs toFun and invFun, combined with @[simps!] on quotientPi. I did not run Lean. I did not check exactly what the simps! projection lemmas look like, so the finding says only what the declarations imply. I am also unsure whether other files rely on the unfolding behaviour. findings.excerpt:
@[simp]
def toFun : ((∀ i, Ms i) ⧸ pi Set.univ p) → ∀ i, Ms i ⧸ p i :=
findings.problem: `toFun` and `invFun` are private-style helper definitions used only to build `quotientPi`. Both carry a bare `@[simp]`, which registers their defining equation as a simp rewrite. Any `toFun p x` or `invFun p y` is therefore unfolded to `quotientPiLift p (fun i => (p i).mkQ) _ x` or `piQuotientLift p (pi Set.univ p) _ _ y`. The simp-normal form is then stated in terms of the internal lifts instead of the public `quotientPi`. The equation lemma for `invFun` also contains the proof term `fun _ => le_comap_single_pi p` and the placeholder function `_`. `quotientPi` is already `@[simps!]`, so its `quotientPi_apply` and `quotientPi_symm_apply` lemmas are the intended interface. The `@[simp]` attributes on the auxiliary defs are a second, competing route. They expose `quotientPi_aux` internals to any downstream `simp` call and depend on the internal definition rather than on a stable statement. Nothing in the file needs them: `left_inv` and `right_inv` call `dsimp only [toFun, invFun]` explicitly.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `toFun` and `invFun`. The explicit `dsimp only [toFun, invFun]` calls in `left_inv` and `right_inv` keep working. If a user-facing simp lemma is needed, state one on `quotientPi` itself, for example `quotientPi p (Quotient.mk x) = fun i => Quotient.mk (x i)`. It can be proved by `rfl`, following `quotientPiLift_mk`. Alternatively, keep the `@[simps!]` output as the only simp interface.
findings.benefit: The simp-normal form is given in terms of the public equivalence `quotientPi` and the generated or hand-stated lemmas, not the internal `quotientPi_aux` lifts. This avoids competing rewrite routes and unwanted unfolding of the auxiliary definitions in downstream goals. It also lets the helper definitions be changed later without breaking simp behaviour.
